title: v4 metric design: decompose tokens into Real-Work (W) vs Hardness (H) vs Consult-overhead (C); win = (H_off−H_on) > C
summary: v1-v3 came out parity because OUTPUT tokens lump 'real work' (writing the solution, ~constant across arms) with 'hardness' (figuring it out: exploration/re-discovery/debugging) — and the orchestrator can ONLY reduce hardness. Those tasks had ~zero hardness → nothing to save → parity. v4 must use a HIGH-HARDNESS task. DECOMPOSITION per arm: W (real-work) ≈ token-size of the final `git diff` in the arm's worktree (the shipped solution; should be ~equal across arms); H (hardness) = total_output_tokens − W (exploration beyond emitting the answer); corroborators = #Read/Grep/Bash(test) calls + #edit-revisions; C (consult overhead, ON only) = cost-weighted(ON cache_read+creation − OFF's) = what ON pays to carry graph context. REFINED WIN CONDITION (pre-registered, frozen): precondition H_off ≥ 2×W (task genuinely hard for OFF — the new guard replacing 'self-solvable=fine'); fairness both arms solve ≥80% (no cap); WIN = cost-weighted (H_off − H_on) > C by margin > noise at n≥8 (saved re-discovery worth more than context carry-cost); corroboration W_on ≈ W_off (≤1.1× — same-size solution, confirms we measured hardness not a different answer). The loop optimizes (H_off − H_on) − C, want >0 with margin. Auto-explains a null: if opus re-derives cheaply, H_off stays small, nothing beats C → 'recorded context rarely pays its carry cost for a strong model' — a real finding. BUILD: bench-arm.js captures W (diff size) before worktree cleanup; bench-report.js computes W/H/C + the inequality + guards; then set_task_metric encodes measure_command=bench harness emitting (H_off−H_on)−C, target>0, guardrail both-solve≥0.8; loop wired with request_guidance FAIRNESS gate (loop proposes task designs, human certifies each is fair/both-solvable before its numbers count) + loop_start budget. Anti-gaming: pre-registered bar + human fairness gate (an advantage-maximizing loop will otherwise rig OFF to fail).
